title: PKSE Knowledge Synthesis Engine: Dedup by Hash Identity — Complex
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] The same technique written twice is one technique: the dedup pipeline normalizes each entry and hashes it, merging hash-identical entries. The desk computes the expected dedup rate from the duplicate distribution — the index shrinks honestly.

Full technical depth. Headline number: Collision odds for 50k entries (128-bit) = 3.673e-30 probability. Every equation below was recomputed at build time; corrected and unverifiable items are labeled, never hidden.
chapter_source: The Perpetual Knowledge Synthesis Engine (PKSE) – Quantifying All Potential Techniques
real_world_basis: Hash-identity dedup is the real, standard method of index cleaning.
signature_version: Signature version: the PKSE dedup desk — the chapter's constant as the cleanliness target, with the perpetual framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: the normalization rules decide the merges — publish them.
math_note: Collision odds for 50k entries (128-bit): 3.673e-30 probability [verified]; Entries after 20% dedup of 50000: 40000 entries [verified]
safety: No hazard; the failure mode is aggressive merging of distinct techniques.
how_it_works: Normalize, hash, merge on hash equality, and report the merge rate. The demo dedups a 50,000-entry crawl.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
